template: Plan and go on a solo dinner date: pick a restaurant, sit down, and stay through one full meal without scrolling your phone the whole time.
Invite [person] out for coffee or tea at a spot you have never been to and stay for at least 30 minutes.
Pick a movie theater and take yourself to see a film alone, buying yourself a snack like you would if you were on a date.
Choose a park or waterfront and go on a sunset walk with [person] or solo, staying out until the sun is fully down.
Pick a dessert-only spot and go out just for dessert either solo or with [person]. No main course, just treats.
Go out for ice cream, frozen yogurt, or a sweet snack and actually sit down to enjoy it instead of eating on the go.
Invite [person] to walk a full loop around a park or neighborhood with you and have phone-free conversation the whole time.
Choose a place with live music and go there for at least one full set, even if you go alone.
Take yourself or [person] to a bookstore and spend at least 20 minutes browsing in silence together before sharing what you each found.
Do a coffee shop hop: visit two different cafés in one evening and order something at both.
Invite [person] to a casual drink (alcoholic or not) at a bar or lounge and sit at the bar instead of a table.
Have a solo movie night at home where you dress like you’re going out, make or order good food, and actually sit and watch start to finish.
Take [person] to a view spot like a rooftop, overlook, or bridge and stay long enough to talk for at least 20 minutes.
Get dressed slightly nicer than usual and walk to a nearby bar, café, or lounge just to sit for one drink or snack by yourself.
Go on a thrift store date with [person]: each of you picks one silly or stylish item for the other to try on.
Do a solo picnic: bring food or takeout to a park, lay out a blanket, and eat there instead of at home.
Plan and go on a cheap date with [person] that costs under a budget you set, focusing on vibe not money.
Take yourself or [person] to a museum or gallery that stays open late and wander through slowly.
Go bowling, play pool, mini golf, or another casual game with [person] or solo against your own score.
Take a long evening walk with [person] or solo with the explicit intention of not checking your phone until you’re home.
Go out for a late-night diner or fast-food run with [person] or solo, sit inside, and eat there instead of in the car.
Do a bookstore date with yourself: buy or pick a book, then go read it in a café for 30 minutes.
Take [person] to a neighborhood neither of you usually visit and explore one whole block together on foot.
Pick a theme for the night such as tacos, pizza, or dessert and hit two different spots that fit the theme.
Invite [person] over or meet up and cook a simple meal together instead of ordering delivery.
Take yourself on a public transport ride to a new stop, get off, find a café, and sit down for a drink.
Plan a daytime date with [person] that isn’t just food: a walk, gallery, park, bookstore, or event plus a drink.
Take yourself or [person] to an arcade or gaming bar and load a small amount of credits, playing at least three games.
Dress in an outfit that makes you feel attractive and go sit at a bar, lounge, or café alone for one drink.
Walk or drive to a scenic spot at night and have a parked-car conversation or solo reflection with music playing quietly.
Take [person] to a place that meant something to you in the past and tell them why it matters.
Go to a touristy spot in your own city and do the cheesy date move of taking a photo there either solo or with [person].
Have a coffee shop work date with yourself: bring a notebook or laptop, order a drink, and stay for at least an hour.
Take [person] to get try-on outfits at a clothing store, giving each other one outfit to try and rating them for fun.
Go out specifically for appetizers or small plates with [person] or solo instead of ordering a full entrée.
Arrange a park hang with [person]: bring a blanket, snacks, and music for at least 45 minutes of chill time.
Take yourself or [person] to an area where there are multiple bars or cafés and pick one at random to go into.
Go to a food truck park or cluster of street food vendors and try at least two different stalls.
Ask [person] out for a walk-and-talk date around a block, park, or waterfront instead of sitting down somewhere.
Treat yourself to getting ready for a date even if you’re solo: shower, outfit, scent, then go out to a public place for 30 minutes.
Take [person] to a late-night dessert spot after 9 PM and sit down inside instead of taking it to go.
Go to a karaoke bar or private room with [person] or solo and sing at least one full song, even if you’re nervous.
Pick a cuisine you’ve rarely or never had and go on a date (solo or with [person]) specifically to try that cuisine.
Have a phone-free dinner with [person] at home or out where both of you keep phones away until the meal is done.
Take yourself on a midday date: go out for lunch alone at a restaurant where you’re seated and served.
Walk with [person] through a part of town with lights, murals, or interesting storefronts and take at least one photo together or separately.
Plan a cheap movie night at home for you and [person] with popcorn, snacks, and a movie you actually sit and watch.
Take yourself to a nice coffee shop or hotel lobby bar and sit down long enough to finish a drink slowly.
Ask [person] to go vintage or thrift shopping with you and each pick one item the other actually buys and keeps.
Walk to a lookout point, hill, bridge, or balcony and share music with [person] using a splitter or one earbud each.
Take yourself to a fancy or bougie spot just for one drink or dessert, then leave like you do this all the time.
Invite [person] to a daytime coffee date and sit outside if possible, staying for at least 30 minutes.
Go to a local festival, street fair, or market and walk the whole thing with [person] or solo.
Have a solo museum date: one ticket, one audio guide if available, and at least 45 minutes of walking and looking.
Take [person] to a place where you can see the city lights at night and stay long enough to actually relax into the view.
Plan a simple, cheap, but thoughtful solo date night at home: cooked meal, candles or lighting, and one movie or album.
Go to a neighborhood with lots of restaurants and physically walk the strip before choosing where to eat, even if you're alone.
Invite [person] to join you at a live comedy show, open mic, or performance and stay until it ends.
Treat yourself to a long walk followed by a sit-down drink or dessert in a different neighborhood than usual.
Have a board game or card game date night with [person] either at home or at a bar or café that offers games.
Take yourself out for brunch on a weekend and sit outside or by a window people-watching.
Invite [person] to a casual foodie date where you share at least two different dishes or small plates.
Go to a rooftop, balcony, or park late enough to see stars or the night sky and stay until you feel your body fully relax.
Have a mall date with [person] or solo where the mission is just to walk the whole mall and people-watch, not shop.
Choose a restaurant you’ve always been too nervous or intimidated to try and finally go, even if it’s just for one dish.
Invite [person] for a walking ice cream date: buy ice cream and walk at least 15 minutes while eating.
Take a solo train, bus, or tram ride at night just to see your city lit up, then hop off one stop early and walk the rest.
Find a local wine bar, tea house, or specialty drink spot and take [person] or yourself there for something you’ve never ordered.
Have a sit-down pizza date, even if it’s just a slice shop: no rushing, eat at the table or counter.
Invite [person] to walk with you across a bridge, overpass, or long walkway and back, talking the whole time.
Take yourself somewhere slightly overdressed for the occasion just for the fun of it and stay out for at least 30 minutes.
Have a cheap date night with [person] where you split fries, a drink, or one cheap meal and sit and talk for 30 minutes.
Drive or ride out to a look-out or scenic pull-off with [person] or alone, and stay until you’ve had at least one real thought about your life.
Go to a bookstore or library with [person] where you each pick one book the other should read and at least read the first chapter together there.
Take yourself on a city night walk specifically to look into the lit windows of bars, cafés, and restaurants as you pass.
Invite [person] to a casual food-court date where you each grab something from different places and then meet back at one table.
Go to a body of water with [person] or solo and sit on the edge or shoreline for at least 20 minutes without scrolling.
Have a solo self-care date at home: long shower or bath, clean outfit, and a meal or dessert you plate nicely for yourself.
Take [person] on a bus or train ride across town and get off at a random stop with lights or shops to walk around.
Plan a late afternoon date that rolls into evening: a walk or activity before dark and food or drinks after.
Take yourself to a restaurant with counter seating and choose the counter instead of a regular table.
Invite [person] to a casual gallery or museum exhibit and discuss your favorite and least favorite piece afterward.
Go to an ice rink, roller rink, or place to skate and skate at least one full song or lap whether you are good at it or not.
Have a solo coffee-and-journal date at a café: one drink and at least one full page of handwriting.
Take [person] to your favorite cheap food spot and order for both of you if they're cool with it.
Walk a full loop around a lake, pond, or very large block as if it’s a slow date with yourself.
Invite [person] to an early morning coffee or breakfast date to see the city before it fully wakes up.
Take yourself to a random restaurant within a set distance that you’ve never been to and order whatever actually sounds best.
Have a ‘no phone at the table’ policy with [person] or solo for an entire meal out, focusing only on the food and the moment.
Take a long walk through a lively strip or downtown area at night with [person] or solo just to soak in the energy.
Go to a nearby town or neighborhood by train, car, or bus and have a mini date there instead of your usual area.
Invite [person] to split a sampler plate, tasting flight, or variety platter with you.
Have a solo ‘get ready with me’ night: pick an outfit, do your grooming, and go somewhere public for at least 45 minutes.
Take [person] for a late-night walk in a safe, well-lit area and talk until one of you mentions being tired.
Go to a food spot that has outdoor seating and stay until the scene around you changes at least once such as sunset to dark or busy to slow.
Invite [person] to a park date where each of you brings one surprise snack or drink for the other.
Have a solo date where you intentionally speak out loud one nice thing about yourself before you leave the house and after you get back.
Take [person] to a photo-worthy spot like a mural, viewpoint, or landmark and ask someone to take a photo of you together.
Go on a day-date with yourself: one activity out of the house plus one sit-down meal or coffee shop stop.
Invite [person] to join you for a full date that includes walking somewhere, sitting and talking somewhere, and eating or drinking something together.
